products.title: Pygmy Seahorse
products.story: Smaller than a fingernail and dressed exactly like its gorgonian home — the pygmy seahorse is the holy grail of macro diving. Finding one is hard. Getting it to hold still is harder.

products.title: Frogfish, Up Close
products.story: All lure, lips, and patience. Meet a frogfish at eye level and you understand why nothing on the reef trusts a sponge.

products.title: Open Wide
products.story: Not a threat — a breath. Morays pump water over their gills mouth-first, which makes every yawn look like a warning. This one held the pose.

products.title: Blue Spots
products.story: A blue-spotted ray wearing colors that shouldn’t exist underwater — until your light brings them back.

products.title: Blue Ribbon
products.story: A ribbon of electric blue hovering over its burrow. Blink and it’s gone; hold your breath and it rises again.

products.title: The Grin
products.story: Porcupinefish always look like they know something you don’t. Shot face-to-face, no zoom tricks — just trust.

products.title: Crinoid Squat Lobster
products.story: Deep inside a feather star’s arms lives a crustacean built of the same colors — a tenant perfectly dressed for its landlord.

products.title: Frogfish & Fairy Lights
products.story: A red frogfish against a bokeh of reef lights — the ocean’s grumpiest face at its most festive.

copy.aboutTeaser: I'm Devyn — a macro photographer who spends as much time as possible below the surface. My favorite subjects are the small ones: shrimp the size of a fingernail, frogfish pretending to be sponges, and everything else most divers swim past.
copy.aboutLong: What started as a way to remember dives became the reason for them. I shoot macro — the tiny, strange, spectacular life that hides on every reef and under every pier piling. My home water is Blue Heron Bridge in Florida, one of the best small-critter dive sites anywhere, and my logbook keeps pulling me back to the Caribbean: Cozumel's walls, Roatán's reefs, and wherever the next small thing is hiding.
